The reaction described is also known as an immediate hemolytic transfusion reaction.
The immediate hemolytic transfusion reaction is a medical emergency.
The immediate hemolytic transfusion reaction results from rapid destruction of donor red blood cells by host antibodies.
The host antibodies involved in the immediate hemolytic transfusion reaction include IgG and IgM.
The immediate hemolytic transfusion reaction is usually related to ABO blood group incompatibility.
The most severe ABO blood group incompatibility often involves group A red cells being given to a patient with group O type blood.
Properdin binds to complement C3 in the donor blood.
Properdin binding to complement C3 facilitates the reaction through the alternate pathway cascade.
The donor cells become coated with IgG.
Coated donor cells are subsequently removed by macrophages in the reticuloendothelial system (RES).
Jaundice may occur as part of the immediate hemolytic transfusion reaction.
Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) may occur as part of the immediate hemolytic transfusion reaction.
The most common cause of the immediate hemolytic transfusion reaction is clerical error.
A clerical error can result in the wrong unit of blood being given to the patient.

The Whistleblower Protection Act of 1989 is Pub. L. 101-12, as amended.
The Whistleblower Protection Act of 1989 is a United States federal law.
The Whistleblower Protection Act of 1989 protects federal whistleblowers who work for the government and report agency misconduct.
A federal agency violates the Whistleblower Protection Act if agency authorities take or threaten to take retaliatory personnel action against any employee or applicant.
A federal agency violates the Whistleblower Protection Act if the retaliatory personnel action is because of disclosure of information by that employee or applicant.
Whistleblowers may file complaints that they believe reasonably evidence a violation of a law, rule or regulation.
Whistleblowers may file complaints about gross mismanagement.

Whistleblowers may file complaints about an abuse of authority.
Whistleblowers may file complaints about a substantial and specific danger to public health or safety.
